findings.problem: Three proofs repeat the same generic-fibre extensionality scaffold. It is `apply genericFibreRestrict_injective_of_flat_of_isSeparated`, then `Subtype.ext`, then `pullback.hom_ext`. The fst branch rewrites with `genericFibreRestrict_coe_comp_fst` twice. The snd branch is closed by `genericFibreRestrict_coe_comp_snd` twice. Each fst branch then proves non-closed-ness of the pulled-back points with the same `rw [pullback.condition, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]; exact specGenericFibreInclusion_ne_closedPoint ...`. See `unit_act` (lines 536-544, 558), `trans_act` (lines 629-640) and `huniv` in `mul_actP` (lines 717-724, 737). `fst_mem_range_sigma1` repeats the same non-closed-point argument. The facts used are that a morphism into `g'` is determined by its restriction to the generic fibre, and that the pullback points lie over the generic point. They are re-derived each time, which makes each proof longer and hides the actual content.
findings.proposed_change: Add two lemmas in the DVR section. (1) `generic_pullback_ne_closedPoint (τ : T ⟶ Spec R') : ∀ p : pullback τ ι, (pullback.fst τ ι ≫ τ).base p ≠ closedPoint R'`. Proof: `rw [pullback.condition, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]; exact specGenericFibreInclusion_ne_closedPoint K' _`. (2) `ext_of_generic [Flat τ] (x y : SchemeHomOver τ g') (h : pullback.fst τ ι ≫ x.1 = pullback.fst τ ι ≫ y.1) : x = y`. Proof: `apply genericFibreRestrict_injective_of_flat_of_isSeparated R' K' g' τ; apply Subtype.ext; apply pullback.hom_ext; · rw [genericFibreRestrict_coe_comp_fst, genericFibreRestrict_coe_comp_fst]; exact h; · rw [genericFibreRestrict_coe_comp_snd, genericFibreRestrict_coe_comp_snd]`. Rewritten uses: `unit_act` becomes `exact congrArg Subtype.val (ext_of_generic K' g' U₁ (schemeHomOverId g') (by <existing fst argument>))`, where the existing argument uses `generic_pullback_ne_closedPoint K' g'` for `hgen`. `trans_act` becomes `exact congrArg Subtype.val (ext_of_generic K' _ T₁ T₂ (comp_actMap_act f X' jY' hjY'₁ act hact hP1 _ (generic_pullback_ne_closedPoint K' _)))`. `huniv` becomes `ext_of_generic K' τ₀ _ _ (<key-derived fst equation>)` with `hg := generic_pullback_ne_closedPoint K' τ₀`. `fst_mem_range_sigma1` can use `generic_pullback_ne_closedPoint K' _` after its `pullback.condition` rewrite. The hypotheses `[IsDomain R'] [IsFractionRing R' K'] [IsSeparated g']` are already in the DVR section, and `Flat τ` is available at each call site (`Smooth g'` for `τ = g'`, `Flat (pullback.snd ...)` for `trans_act`, and the `haveI : Flat τ₀` for `huniv`).
findings.benefit: Each of the three proofs loses its identical 5-6 line scaffold. A reader sees only the mathematically meaningful goal: two morphisms agree once pulled back to the generic fibre. The generic-fibre/closed-point bookkeeping is stated once, so any change to the restriction API needs one edit instead of four.

findings.problem: `mem_range_sigma1_of_ne` and the local `hcl` inside `mem_range_sigma1_of_maximal` both prove the same fact. For `q` in `pullback (g' ≫ sMap R R') (sMap R R')`, the point `g'.base (fst q)` is the closed point exactly when `snd q` is. Each proof builds the same `e` from `pullback.condition`, expands `Scheme.Hom.comp_apply` three times, and applies `sMap_base_eq_closedPoint_iff` twice (lines 254-259 and 276-281). `mem_range_sigma1_of_ne` uses only the forward direction. Only `mem_range_sigma1_of_maximal` names the statement, as a `have` buried in a proof, so it cannot be reused.
findings.proposed_change: Before `mem_range_sigma1_of_ne`, state a lemma `base_fst_eq_closedPoint_iff [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing R'] [Module.Finite R R'] (q : ↑(pullback (g' ≫ sMap R R') (sMap R R'))) : g'.base ((pullback.fst (g' ≫ sMap R R') (sMap R R')).base q) = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R' ↔ (pullback.snd (g' ≫ sMap R R') (sMap R R')).base q = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R'`. Its proof is the current `hcl` proof. Then `mem_range_sigma1_of_ne` becomes `rw [mem_range_sigma1_iff]; apply hjY'₁; intro hc; exact hq ((base_fst_eq_closedPoint_iff q).1 hc)`. In `mem_range_sigma1_of_maximal`, `hcl` is replaced by the lemma and the remaining steps use `(base_fst_eq_closedPoint_iff _).2 hb` and `(base_fst_eq_closedPoint_iff _).1`/`.2` in `hb'c`. The lemma needs `g'` and `R R'` as variables in the Density section, which already supplies `[IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing R'] [Module.Finite R R']`.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated 7-line argument that mixes pullback commutation with the integral-extension closed-point criterion. It gives the key fact a name and statement that can be checked at a glance, and it shortens both density lemmas to their real content, which is the open-immersion range argument.
